note: v1, written: SODIUM. Slowcore waltz into a shoegaze wall (the style board's t4 row): the orange sodium streetlights left on all night. 3/4 at 72 bpm, E minor; the last movement in G major. 7:22, six movements. I HUM: the mains hum (100/200/300 Hz), a ballast's buzz, a failing lamp's relay ticking, one ebow note swelling. II WALTZ: a clean Starcaster waltz (bass note, then the chord in eighths), a fretless, brushes; an ebow sings THE WALTZ. III BLOOM: reverse swells into each phrase, a second guitar gliding the theme an octave down, the ebow answering a third above, brushes to sticks and a snare roll into the wall. IV WALL in four 12-bar stages: chorused crunch guitars strumming eighths L/R, an m8 fuzz rig, a supersaw pad, heavy 6/8 drums with tom fills, sub; then the theme buried in a wordless choir; then a glimpse of the major (G-major changes, the ride doubling); then the drop (fuzz, kick, floor tom) and the full wall back. V FLICKER: the wall bus gated on seeded irregular sixteenths, failing more and more, stuttered, tape-stopped. VI LIGHTS OUT: the waltz in G major on a drowned piano with the clean guitar, the lamps switching off one by one (a thunk and a click each), the hum stepping down to nothing. Levels: true_peak, -18.5 LUFS, PLR 17.3, true peak -1.19 dBTP, run 1; section levels -32 (hum) to -17 dB (wall). compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: 89.512/89.852/89.914/94.249 (structure 75-78, 100 on seed 29: the detector cuts the waltz and bloom into 4-bar pieces). A simpler wall read 90.16 on seed 0 but looped for 48 bars.
next: structure 75-78 (20 sections: the waltz/bloom cut every 4 bars, the wall and the end read as single blocks); spectrum 84 (2-3 kHz +5 from the crunch guitars, the top -5..-8); flow in from Night Freight (40 dB jump at 97 Hz: the hum).

note: v2, written: THE LAMP WARMS UP, THE WALL IN STAGES, LIGHTS OUT IN FOUR. The lamp starts as sodium lamps do: the ballast buzz and the relay first, the hum entering a bar later (the in-join from Night Freight's waves: a 40.7 -> 21 dB level jump). The wall's stages are now distinct: bare strums and fuzz with no pad; then the pad and the buried choir; then the major glimpse, the strums tremolo-picked in 16ths for a shimmer; then the drop and the return. Lights out unfolds in four: the drowned piano alone with the waltz in G; the clean guitar, fretless and brushes join; the ebow's last line over them; the piano and the hum alone as the last lamps go off, the last one in the bar before the end, with a 1 s tail and no dead air into Leave the Lights On. The wall bus's 2.4 kHz comes down 4 dB (the crunch guitars) and the master's top up 3 dB from 8 kHz. compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: v1 89.512/89.852/89.915/94.251 -> v2 94.607/94.807/94.956/94.899 (structure 75-78 -> 98-100: the lights-out stages break the long last block; spectrum 84 -> 86; flow 33 -> 40).
